replies.text: That trans-Atlantic connection is one of the coolest parts of the story. replies.author: @HiddenCanada
replies.text: Morocco does connect into the broader Paleozoic mountain-building story. The Anti-Atlas and Moroccan Meseta were affected by the same late Paleozoic collision that helped assemble Pangaea, and parts of that system are considered counterparts to the Appalachian–Ouachita belt. The modern Atlas Mountains, though, were largely uplifted much later, so they’re not simply a direct continuation of the Appalachians. I probably could’ve added a quick Morocco mention for context.
